title: Enhanced diagrams, spaces and homotopy coherent cones
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and use simplicial sets as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set]. The standard simplex $\Delta^n$ has $m$-simplices the weakly increasing maps $[m]\to[n]$; its operators are precomposition, and its horn $\Lambda_i^n$ is the simplicial subset consisting of maps whose image omits some vertex other than $i$, equivalently the union of the faces other than the $i$th face. An enhanced category means a quasicategory: a simplicial set $\mathscr C$ in which every map $\Lambda_i^n\to\mathscr C$, $0<i<n$, extends to $\Delta^n$. An edge is an equivalence when it has an inverse with both inverse equations witnessed by $2$-simplices. A space is a Kan complex: every map $\Lambda_i^n\to S$, with $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, extends to $\Delta^n$. Thus outer horns are included, but no nonemptiness condition from dimension zero is imposed. Spaces and their maps are considered up to weak homotopy equivalence. All simplicial products and pullbacks below are formed degree by degree, with operators acting on each coordinate. A weak homotopy equivalence of simplicial sets means a map inducing a bijection on components and isomorphisms on every based homotopy group after geometric realization. Geometric realization is the quotient of $\coprod_{n\geq0}K_n\times|\Delta^n|$ with the quotient topology, giving each $K_n$ the discrete topology, by the identifications $(K(\alpha)(u),t)\sim(u,|\alpha|(t))$ for every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, $u\in K_n$ and $t\in|\Delta^m|$. Here $|\alpha|(t)_j=\sum_{\alpha(i)=j}t_i$, and $|\Delta^n|=\{(t_0,\ldots,t_n)\in\mathbb R^{n+1}:t_i\geq0,\ \sum_i t_i=1\}$. Here components mean path components of the realization; for $r\geq1$ and $t\in|T|$, write $\pi_r(|T|,t)$ for homotopy classes relative to the boundary of continuous maps $([0,1]^r,\partial[0,1]^r)\to(|T|,t)$, with multiplication by concatenation in the first coordinate. The map on these groups is postcomposition with the realized map, for every base point in the source realization. Weakly contractible means that the map to the one-point simplicial set $\Delta^0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence; throughout, "contractible" for a space has this meaning.

For a small ordinary category $I$, its nerve $N(I)$ has $n$-simplices the functors $[n]\to I$, with restriction as simplicial operators. For a small simplicial set $K$ define $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)_n=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sSet}}(K\times\Delta^n,\mathscr C)$. For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, its operator sends $h$ to $h\circ(\mathrm{id}_K\times\Delta(\alpha))$. Objects of this simplicial set are coherent diagrams, edges are coherent transformations, and its higher simplices retain their compatibilities. The full subcategory on specified objects contains exactly the simplices whose vertices are specified objects. Write $\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{eq}}(K,\mathscr C)$ for the full subcategory on diagrams carrying every edge of $K$ to an equivalence. The constant-diagram map $\Delta_K$ is induced by $K\to\Delta^0$; evaluation at a vertex is restriction to that vertex.

For a map of Kan complexes $f:A\to B$ and a vertex $b\in B$, its homotopy fiber over $b$ means the space modeled by $A\times_{B,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,B}\{b\}$; its objects are a point $a$ and a 1-simplex of $B$ from $f(a)$ to $b$, with the higher simplices of these data. For objects $x,y$ of a quasicategory, use the mapping space with $n$-simplices the maps $\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathscr C$ whose restriction to the entire initial face $\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n\}}$ is the constant simplex at $x$, and whose last vertex is $y$. Simplicial operators are induced by extending each weakly increasing map $[m]\to[n]$ to $[m+1]\to[n+1]$ by sending the new last vertex to the new last vertex. This is the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathscr C}(x,y)$. An enhanced functor is a simplicial map between the specified quasicategories. It is fully faithful if the induced maps of these mapping simplicial sets are weak homotopy equivalences. A functor equivalence has a quasi-inverse and coherent natural equivalences of the two composites with the identity; a coherent natural equivalence is an equivalence edge in the corresponding functor simplicial set, using the two inverse-triangle witnesses above. The core is the simplicial subset consisting of simplices all of whose edges are equivalences.

For $F:K\to\mathscr C$, a cone with apex $x$ is a coherent transformation $\lambda:\Delta_Kx\to F$; put $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathscr C)$ and define the coherent comma cone category by the simplicial pullback $\mathscr C\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\{F\}$, where $\mathscr C\to D$ is $\Delta_K$. Explicitly an $n$-simplex is a pair $a:\Delta^n\to\mathscr C$, $b:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to D$ with $b|_{\Delta^n\times\{0\}}=\Delta_Ka$ and $b|_{\Delta^n\times\{1\}}$ constant at $F$, with simplicial operators given by restriction. Thus morphisms retain their compatibility homotopies. Denote this category by $(\Delta_K\downarrow F)$. A cone is limiting if it is terminal in this category. Here terminal means that the mapping space into it from every object is contractible. The space of limiting cones means the core of the full subcategory of limiting cones, allowing the apex to vary. Here an initial object is one whose mapping space to each object is contractible. Dually cocones are transformations $F\to\Delta_Kx$, the cocone category is $\{F\}\times_{D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,D}\mathscr C$, and colimiting cocones are its initial objects. The notations $\operatorname{holim}F$ and $\operatorname{hocolim}F$ mean the apices of such cones and cocones when they exist, without choosing any data from an unproved mere existence theorem.

source.place: Lecture II, Definitions 2.1 and 2.2 and basic facts (1)-(7), printed pp. 13-15, for quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets, equivalences, cores and spaces. Cone/comma and limit terminology is agent-specified; WANTED: an archived infinity-categorical cone/limit reference. The right-pinched convention is checked against online Kerodon, Construction 4.6.5.1 (Tag 01KX) and Remark 4.6.5.2 in Subsection 4.6.5 (Tag 01KW); the whole initial face is constant. The displayed comma category is specified explicitly by a simplicial pullback. The explicit simplicial operators, degreewise products/pullbacks, realization quotient relation, and based cube-homotopy convention are agent-specified expansions of the constructions, rather than additional theorem assertions.
